newsitem.title: CAMEROON: Cameroon opposition discusses election alliance.
newsitem.headline: Cameroon opposition discusses election alliance.

text.p: Cameroon's main opposition parties are discussing forming an electoral alliance to confront President Paul Biya and his ruling party in parliamentary and presidential elections later this year, party officials say.

Leaders of the Social Democratic Front (SDF) and the National Union for Democracy and Progress (UNDP) outlined their desire for an electoral front at the annual congress of the National Union in its northern stronghold of Ngaoundere.
"We have reached a point of no-return for an electoral alliance," Bello Bouba Maigari, leader of the more moderate National Union, told the closing session at the weekend.
"We of the opposition owe this alliance to the Cameroon people who have suffered under the 14 years leadership of Paul Biya and we have to change this trend," he said.
SDF leader John Fru Ndi, runner-up to Biya in the 1992 presidential election, echoed Maigari's call.

"The moment has now come for the opposition to come together and flush out Paul Biya and his cohorts... before they plunge this country further into total political and economic chaos," he told the congress.

Cameroon's opposition formed an alliance, the Union for Change, in 1992 but it collapsed in the run-up to the presidential election. Maigari came third in that poll with Biya benefiting from a divided opposition vote to win a third term.
Biya's Democratic Rally of the Cameroon People (RDPC) won a majority in parliament with support of a minor paarty.
Party officials spoke of broad agreement on consensus candidates for parliamentary elections which must be held by March. Presidential elections must be held by October.
